options.text: ECG shows ST-segment elevation in leads V2-V4.
Client reports persistent 7/10 crushing chest pain despite receiving sublingual nitroglycerin.
Oral temperature 98.6°F (37°C).
Troponin I level 0.8 ng/mL (normal range <0.04 ng/mL).
Capillary refill time less than 3 seconds.
Blood pressure 90/58 mmHg.
Client reports a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
Respiratory rate 18 breaths/min with unlabored respirations.

rationale.golden_rule: The nurse must prioritize immediate assessment of chest pain characteristics and vital signs to identify potential myocardial infarction and initiate life-saving interventions.
rationale.answer_analysis: ST-segment elevation on the ECG (option A) is a hallmark sign of a ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), indicating transmural ischemia and requiring immediate intervention, such as percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Persistent crushing chest pain despite nitroglycerin (option B) signifies ongoing myocardial ischemia and the ineffectiveness of initial interventions, necessitating further assessment and treatment. An elevated Troponin I level of 0.8 ng/mL (option D), well above the normal range (<0.04 ng/mL), confirms myocardial cell damage and is diagnostic of an MI. Blood pressure 90/58 mmHg (option F) indicates hypotension, which can be a serious complication of MI, such as cardiogenic shock or right ventricular infarction, and requires urgent evaluation and intervention.
